newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE to form firm for satellite project in January.
newsitem.headline: UAE to form firm for satellite project in January.

text.p: A United Arab Emirates-based shareholding company is expected to be formed next month to run a major satellite project for mobile communications to be operating by the turn of the century, a UAE minister said on Friday.

"We have reached an advanced stage regarding the formation of the company that will own and operate the al-Thurayya project," said Ahmed bin Humaid al-Tayer, Minister of State for Finance and Industrial Affairs and acting Communications Minister.
"We expect an announcement on it during next January," he told the official news agency WAM after returning from a meeting of Arab League communication ministers in Cairo.
He said the meeting recommended Arab countries use the services to be offered by the planned company, al-Thurayya for Satellite Communications.

Etisalat, the UAE's telecommunications giant, expects the company to have a starting capital of $25 million, to be raised to $500 million within six months. Total costs for the project would be around $800 million, officials said.
The system will provide services to UAE users of two-way mobile telephones compatible with the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM).
It will make services available to remote sea and rural areas and will cover most Arab states, parts of the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, North Africa and parts of Europe.
Etisalat will hold 26 percent of Thurayya's shares while 51 percent will go to UAE nationals and leading local investment and financial firms, officials said.

Arab Satellite Communications Organisation (Arabsat) and other regional telecommunications departments will be offered the rest. Arabsat, which operates satellite communications for Arab countries, is jointly owned by 21 Arab states.
Two French and one American telecommunication manufacturers have made offers for the project but the candidate has yet to be chosen.
